subject: Chemistry
title: Dalton's Atomic Theory Replaces Alchemy
description: A fast breakdown of Dalton's Atomic Theory Replaces Alchemy for builders.

hook.text: In 1803, John Dalton proposed that all matter is made of indivisible atoms—killing the idea of elemental transmutation.

buildup.text: Dalton noticed that elements combine in fixed ratios by weight. This made no sense unless matter came in tiny packets.

discovery.text: Each element has unique atoms with a specific weight. Compounds form when atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios.

twist.text: If lead and gold have different atoms, you can't rearrange qualities to transform one into the other. Alchemy was dead.

climax.text: Dalton's table of atomic weights—though many were wrong—became the starting point for all of modern chemistry.

punchline.text: Fixed atoms, fixed weights, no transmutation. Science replaced 2,000 years of alchemy.

quiz.question: How did Dalton's atomic theory disprove alchemy?
options: If elements have unique atoms, you can't simply transform one element into another
He showed that gold doesn't actually exist as an element
He proved that all metals are made of the same atom

details.summary: John Dalton proposed in 1803 that all matter consists of indivisible atoms of specific elements, each with characteristic mass. His atomic theory explained chemical combination in fixed ratios and definitively replaced two millennia of alchemy's four-elements framework with a testable.
details.whyItMatters: Dalton's atomic theory provided the theoretical foundation for all modern chemistry and physics. It enabled prediction of chemical reactions, stoichiometric calculations, and ultimately the periodic table.
takeaways: Dalton proposed that each element consists of identical indivisible atoms
Atoms combine in fixed whole-number ratios to form compounds
His theory provided a quantitative framework that replaced alchemical ideas

faq.question: How did Dalton's atomic theory explain what alchemy could not?
faq.answer: Dalton explained that elements are fundamentally different because their atoms have different masses. Transmutation fails because you cannot change an atom's fundamental nature through chemical means..

faq.question: What evidence did Dalton use to support his atomic theory?
faq.answer: Dalton observed that elements combine in fixed mass ratios and proposed that this occurs because atoms combine in fixed number ratios. He compiled the first table of relative atomic weights..
